newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea's top union body to call strike on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Korea's top union body to call strike on Saturday.

text.p: South Korea's main union body will call for a strike on Saturday in protest at the passage of a new labour law, officials at the Federation of Korean Trade Unions said on Thursday.
They said a decision on how long to extend the industrial action would be announced on Friday. Transport workers would be excluded from the stoppage.
Representatives of union affiliates will meet in Seoul on Friday to plan action, one official said. The federation claims membership of 1.2 million workers at 800 companies.
Most South Koreans work a half day on Saturday.

Earlier, the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, the country's second largest umbrella union body, called out all its 500,000 workers immediately over the labour law that allows employers to lay off workers.
The law was passed by the ruling New Korea Party at a dawn session of the National Assembly on Thursday when no opposition deputies were present.
